resolved.title: 静态及动态内存
resolved.description:
[s0l0!-header][h1]Static & Dynamic Memory[/h1][/s0l0!-header] 

To be successful as a C++ programmer, it's essential to have a good understanding of how [b]dynamic memory[/b] works.
In a C++ program, memory is divided into two parts:
[b]The stack[/b]: All of your local variables take up memory from the stack.
[b]The heap[/b]: Unused program memory that can be used when the program runs to [b]dynamically [/b]allocate the memory.

Many times, you are not aware in advance how much memory you will need to store particular information in a defined variable and the size of required memory can be determined at run time.
You can allocate memory at run time within the heap for the variable of a given type using the [b]new [/b]operator, which returns the address of the space allocated. [code format="cpp" ][b]new [/b]int;[/code]
[note]This allocates the memory size necessary for storing an [b]integer [/b]on the [b]heap[/b], and returns that address.[/note]

content.text:
要想成为一名成功的C++程序员，必须充分了解**动态内存**的工作原理。

在C++程序中，内存分为两部分：
1. **栈**：在函数内部声明的所有变量都将占用栈内存。
2. **堆**：程序中未使用的内存，在程序运行时可用于**动态**分配内存。

很多时候，你事先并不知道需要多少内存来存储定义变量中的特定信息，所需内存的大小在运行时才能确定。

此时，你可以在运行时为给定类型的变量在**堆**上分配内存，使用**new**操作符，该操作符返回新分配空间的地址。如：

You can allocate memory at run time within the heap for the variable of a given type using the **new **operator, which returns the address of the space allocated.

resolved.description:
[s0l0!-header][h1]Dynamic Memory[/h1][/s0l0!-header] 

The allocated address can be stored in a [b]pointer[/b], which can then be dereferenced to access the variable.
[s0l0!-header][b]Example:[/b][/s0l0!-header] [code format="cpp" ]int *p = [b]new [/b]int;
*p = 5;[/code]
We have dynamically allocated memory for an integer, and assigned it a value of 5.
[note]The pointer [b]p[/b] is stored in the [b]stack [/b]as a local variable, and holds the [b]heap[/b]'s allocated address as its value. The value of 5 is stored at that address in the heap.[/note]

resolved.title: 动态内存释放
resolved.description:
[s0l0!-header][h1]Dynamic Memory[/h1][/s0l0!-header] 

For local variables on the [b]stack[/b], managing memory is carried out automatically.
On the [b]heap[/b], it's necessary to manually handle the dynamically allocated memory, and use the [b]delete [/b]operator to free up the memory when it's no longer needed. [code format="cpp" ][b]delete [/b]pointer;[/code]
This statement releases the memory pointed to by [b]pointer[/b].

[s0l0!-header][b]For example:[/b][/s0l0!-header] [code format="cpp" codeId="225"]int *p = [b]new [/b]int; // request memory
*p = 5; // store value

cout << *p << endl; // use value

[b]delete [/b]p; // free up the memory[/code]
[note]Forgetting to free up memory that has been allocated with the [b]new [/b]keyword will result in memory leaks, because that memory will stay allocated until the program shuts down.[/note]
resolved.description_en:
[s0l0!-header][h1]Dynamic Memory[/h1][/s0l0!-header] 

For local variables on the [b]stack[/b], managing memory is carried out automatically.
On the [b]heap[/b], it's necessary to manually handle the dynamically allocated memory, and use the [b]delete [/b]operator to free up the memory when it's no longer needed. [code format="cpp" ][b]delete [/b]pointer;[/code]
This statement releases the memory pointed to by [b]pointer[/b].

[s0l0!-header][b]For example:[/b][/s0l0!-header] [code format="cpp" codeId="225"]int *p = [b]new [/b]int; // request memory
*p = 5; // store value

cout << *p << endl; // use value

[b]delete [/b]p; // free up the memory[/code]
[note]Forgetting to free up memory that has been allocated with the [b]new [/b]keyword will result in memory leaks, because that memory will stay allocated until the program shuts down.[/note]

content.text:
对于**栈**上的局部变量，内存管理是自动进行的。

在**堆**上，就有必要手动处理动态分配的内存，并在不再需要时使用**delete**操作符释放内存。
content.text_html:
For local variables on the stack, managing memory is carried out automatically. On the heap, it's necessary to manually handle the dynamically allocated memory, and use the **delete **operator to free up the memory when it's no longer needed.

对于栈上的局部变量，管理内存是自动进行的。 在堆上，有必要手动处理动态分配的内存，并在不再需要时使用删除**操作符来释放内存。

resolved.title: 悬空指针
resolved.description:
[s0l0!-header][h1]Dangling Pointers[/h1][/s0l0!-header] 

The [b]delete [/b]operator frees up the memory allocated for the variable, but does not delete the pointer itself, as the pointer is stored on the stack.

Pointers that are left pointing to non-existent memory locations are called [b]dangling pointers[/b].
[s0l0!-header][b]For example:[/b][/s0l0!-header] [code format="cpp" codeId="226"]int *p = [b]new [/b]int; // request memory
*p = 5; // store value

[b]delete [/b]p; // free up the memory
// now p is a dangling pointer

p = [b]new [/b]int; // reuse for a new address[/code]
[note]The [b]NULL [/b]pointer is a constant with a value of zero that is defined in several of the standard libraries, including iostream.
It's a good practice to assign NULL to a pointer variable when you declare it, in case you do not have exact address to be assigned. A pointer assigned NULL is called a [b]null pointer[/b]. For example: int *ptr = NULL;[/note]
resolved.description_en:
[s0l0!-header][h1]Dangling Pointers[/h1][/s0l0!-header] 

The [b]delete [/b]operator frees up the memory allocated for the variable, but does not delete the pointer itself, as the pointer is stored on the stack.

Pointers that are left pointing to non-existent memory locations are called [b]dangling pointers[/b].
[s0l0!-header][b]For example:[/b][/s0l0!-header] [code format="cpp" codeId="226"]int *p = [b]new [/b]int; // request memory
*p = 5; // store value

[b]delete [/b]p; // free up the memory
// now p is a dangling pointer

p = [b]new [/b]int; // reuse for a new address[/code]
[note]The [b]NULL [/b]pointer is a constant with a value of zero that is defined in several of the standard libraries, including iostream.
It's a good practice to assign NULL to a pointer variable when you declare it, in case you do not have exact address to be assigned. A pointer assigned NULL is called a [b]null pointer[/b]. For example: int *ptr = NULL;[/note]

content.text:
**delete**操作符释放了为该变量分配的内存，但并没有删除指针本身，因为指针是存储在栈中的。

指向不存在的内存位置的指针被称为悬空指针(**dangling pointers**)。

The **delete **operator frees up the memory allocated for the variable, but does not delete the pointer itself, as the pointer is stored on the stack.

Pointers that are left pointing to non-existent memory locations are called dangling pointers. For example:

删除操作符释放了为该变量分配的内存，但并没有删除指针本身，因为指针是存储在堆栈中的。

content.text:
**NULL**指针是一个值为0的常量，在几个标准库（包括iostream）中定义。

当你声明一个指针变量时，将其赋值为NULL是一个很好的做法，以防你没有确切的地址要被赋值。一个被赋值为NULL的指针被称为**空指针**。例如：`int *ptr = NULL`。
content.text_html:
The **NULL **pointer is a constant with a value of zero that is defined in several of the standard libraries, including iostream. It's a good practice to assign NULL to a pointer variable when you declare it, in case you do not have exact address to be assigned. A pointer assigned NULL is called a null pointer. For example: int *ptr = NULL;

resolved.title: 数组动态分配
resolved.description:
[s0l0!-header][h1]Dynamic Memory[/h1][/s0l0!-header] 

Dynamic memory can also be allocated for arrays.
[s0l0!-header][b]For example:[/b][/s0l0!-header] [code format="cpp" codeId="227"]int *p = NULL; // Pointer initialized with null
p = [b]new [/b]int[20]; // Request memory
[b]delete [][/b] p; // Delete array pointed to by p[/code]
Note the [b]brackets [/b]in the syntax.
[note]Dynamic memory allocation is useful in many situations, such as when your program depends on input. As an example, when your program needs to read an image file, it doesn't know in advance the size of the image file and the memory necessary to store the image.[/note]
